raw_response:
I have 9.5 mu and only two people in the household, so I will keep the plan simple and steady. I will put 7 mu into my usual wheat-maize rotation and leave 2.5 mu for cotton, because that matches the way I have farmed here for years and it spreads my risk across grain and cash crop. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to protect wheat at key stages, give maize water in summer heat if rain is short, and keep cotton from stalling after planting and during boll setting. I am 65, so I will not choose a management style that is too complicated or too labor-heavy. I will use better seed where it matters, put on enough fertilizer to hold yield but not waste money, use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage, and spray cotton more than wheat and maize because cotton usually needs closer pest control. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to get a stable harvest from land I know well.
